prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: production pixel-art overworld trainer sprite sheet for a Pokémon Black/White-inspired Nintendo DS 2.5D game.
Create a NEW redrawn sheet of the ONE specified character, preserving the identity in reference images 1 (legacy walking) and 2 (legacy back). Reference image 3 is the authentic Black/White visual style only; reference image 4 is the approved Leaf sheet and is the exact layout, pixel density and scale-consistency target. Do not turn the character into Leaf, Hilbert or Hilda.
Layout: portrait 768×1024 transparent canvas, EXACTLY 3 columns ×4 equally spaced rows, 12 whole-body sprites, one per slot. Use transparent space between every slot. Row1 all facing DOWN/toward viewer; row2 all facing UP/away (only back of head visible); row3 all facing LEFT, row4 all facing RIGHT. Columns: left-leg walking step, neutral standing with both feet planted, right-leg walking step. Keep the same top-down 3/4 camera and same head/body scale in all frames. Distinct foot/arm positions so walk animation reads clearly.
Pixel style: genuine chunky low-resolution DS-era sprite construction, approximately 20–24 pixels wide ×28 pixels tall inside a logical32×32 cell then nearest-neighbor enlarged8× for delivery, dark1logical-pixel outlines, compact muted palettes, crisp square pixels, minimal2–3tone shading, large head and short body in the exact proportions of the Leaf sheet. No smooth gradients, antialiasing, tall doll anatomy, elaborate modern illustration or painted texture.
Actual transparent alpha background. No ground shadows, scene, text, labels, grid lines, borders, logos, props outside the costume, extra characters, duplicated frames or cropping. Every frame has clear transparent margin on all sides.
Subject: Gloria: girl with brown bob-length hair, round dark green Scottish beret with a small pom-pom, gray/green long-sleeved tunic sweater dress with contrasting collar, brown shoes and dark socks, a compact brown backpack. Keep her distinctive beret and bob haircut, matching the reference.
